description:
Save durable facts to persistent memory that survive across sessions. Memory is injected into every future turn, so keep entries compact and high-signal.

HOW: make ALL your changes to one target in ONE call. The batch applies atomically and the char limit is checked only on the FINAL result — so a single call can remove/patch stale entries to free room AND add new ones, even when an add alone would overflow. If an add is rejected as full (the current entries are shown), reissue it as ONE such batch. The response reports current/limit chars and confirms completion; one batch call finishes the update, so don't repeat it.

WHEN: only for facts that apply to EVERY session regardless of task: who the user is, stable environment facts, standing conventions with no task home. Anything learned while doing a task (procedures, pitfalls, and the user's preferences and corrections for that kind of work) belongs in the task's skill via skill_manage, where it loads only when relevant.

SKIP: trivial/obvious info, easily re-discovered facts, raw data dumps, task progress, completed-work logs, temporary TODO state (use session_search for those). Reusable procedures belong in a skill, not memory.
name: memory

operations.description: A single change is a one-item list.

content.description: Required for 'add' and 'patch'. For 'add', the new entry. For 'patch', the text that replaces old_text; the rest of the entry is kept.

old_text.description: REQUIRED for 'patch' and 'remove': text from one entry. 'patch' replaces exactly this span (it must occur once in the entry); 'remove' deletes the whole entry. Omit for 'add'.

target.description: 'user' = who the user is (name, role, preferences, style). 'memory' = your notes (environment, conventions, tool quirks, lessons).
